dhp235:1: Now art thou as a withered leaf; death’s messengers await thee;
dhp235:3: Thou standest at the point of departure; thou hast no provisions for the journey.
dhp236:1: Make for thyself an island; haste thee to struggle; be wise;
dhp236:3: When thy infirmities have been blown away, and thou hast freed thyself from the evil passions, thou shalt go to the heavenly place of the Elect.
dhp237:1: Thy life is now brought to a close; thou art come into the presence of Death;
dhp237:3: Thou hast no abiding-place by the way; thou hast no provisions for the journey.
dhp238:1: Make for thyself an island; haste thee to struggle; be wise.
dhp238:3: When thy infirmities have been blown away, and thou hast freed thyself from the evil passions, thou shalt no more come unto birth and old age.
dhp239:1: One after another, little by little, time after time, a wise man
dhp239:3: Should blow away his own impurities, even as a smith blows away the impurities of silver.
dhp240:1: Even as rust which springs from iron no sooner appears than it eats away the iron,
dhp240:3: Precisely so in the case of transgressors, their own evil deeds bring them to an evil end.
dhp241:1: Non-repetition mars the Sacred Word; inactivity mars the household life;
dhp241:3: Sloth is a blemish on beauty; heedlessness is a blemish on the watchman.
dhp242:1: Lewdness is a blemish on a woman; niggardliness is a blemish on a giver;
dhp242:3: Evil ways are blemishes, both in this world and the next.
dhp243:1: But worse than any ordinary blemish, the worst, indeed, of all blemishes, is ignorance;
dhp243:3: Rid yourselves of this blemish, monks, and be without blemish.
dhp244:1: Easy is the life of the man who is shameless, bold like a crow, a backbiter,
dhp245:1: Hard is the life of the man who is modest, ever seeking what is pure,
dhp245:3: Free from attachment, contained, blameless in conduct, possessed of vision clear.
dhp246:1: He that destroys life, he that utters falsehood,
dhp246:3: He that takes what is not given to him in this world, he that goes in unto another man’s wife,
dhp247:1: And the man that is addicted to the drinking of liquor and spirits,
dhp247:3: Such a man, even in this present world, digs up his own root.
dhp248:1: Know this, O man, that the unrestrained are fallen upon evil ways;
dhp248:3: Let not greed and wrongdoing subject thee to suffering for long.
dhp249:1: People give according to their faith, according to their pleasure;
dhp249:3: Whoever allows himself to be annoyed because food and drink are given to others,
dhp249:5: Such a man will not attain Tranquillity either by day or by night.
dhp250:1: But if a man will exterminate discontent, and tear it out by the roots, and utterly destroy it.
dhp250:3: Then he will attain Tranquillity both by day and by night.
dhp251:1: There is no fire like lust, there is no grip like hatred,
dhp251:3: There is no snare like delusion, there is no river like Craving.
dhp252:1: Easy to see are the flaws of another, but hard to see are one’s own.
dhp252:3: For a man winnows the defects of others like chaff,
dhp252:5: But covers his own, even as a dishonest gambler covers a losing throw.
dhp253:1: If a man look to find flaws in another, if he be minded ever to find fault,
dhp253:3: The Impurities increase within him; such a man is far from Destruction of the Impurities.
dhp254:1: There is no path through the air; no outsider is a monk;
dhp254:3: Mankind delights in the Hindrances; the Tathāgatas are free from the Hindrances.
dhp255:1: There is no path through the air; no outsider is a monk;
dhp255:3: The Aggregates are not eternal; there is no variableness in the Buddhas.
